skill.description: Design paid-ad A/B/n and incrementality tests from a brief or exported results. It produces a hypothesis, variant matrix, sizing plan, and an evidence-based read-out without making business decisions automatically.
skill.summary: Plan and interpret paid-ad experiments with clear ownership rules.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: All 35 static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, relative documentation links, metadata, or the decimal alpha notation. The sole documented command runs a fixed local statistical helper and contains no evidence of network access, arbitrary code execution, data exfiltration, or prompt injection. The skill also explicitly treats exported CSV content as untrusted data and requires consent before saving results.

remediation.issue: Static analysis misclassifies Markdown backticks and relative documentation links as command execution and path traversal.
remediation.suggestion: Replace inline backticks in non-code prose with plain text where practical, or add scanner-aware annotations for Markdown examples and cross-references.

remediation.issue: The local experiment helper is presented as a shell command with placeholder arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Document that arguments must be passed as separate, validated values and never interpolated into a shell string.

remediation.issue: The consent-gated memory path contains a date and topic placeholder.
remediation.suggestion: Specify a filename sanitization rule that restricts topics to safe filename characters before writing saved summaries.

content.value_statement: Paid-ad tests can produce misleading results when variables, thresholds, and decision ownership are unclear. This skill creates structured test plans and interprets exported results with separate statistical and practical-effect checks.
actual_capabilities: Creates a falsifiable hypothesis and a one-variable-per-variant test matrix.
Plans primary, secondary, and guardrail metrics for paid-ad and landing-page tests.
Estimates sample size, duration, alpha, power, and minimum detectable effect requirements.
Interprets user-provided exposure and conversion exports with effect and uncertainty reporting.
Separates statistical detection from practical business relevance.
Returns an undecided result when no owner-approved action rule exists.
limitations: It uses only the brief and exported data that the user provides.
It does not create ad copy, creative assets, or landing-page variants.
It does not connect to ad-platform APIs by default.
It does not make business decisions without a precommitted owner and rule.

use_cases.title: Plan a landing-page test
use_cases.description: Define a controlled hero or call-to-action test with metrics, sample targets, duration, and guardrails.

use_cases.title: Assess creative test results
use_cases.description: Read a finished creative experiment export and report effect size, uncertainty, and practical-effect status.

use_cases.title: Design an incrementality study
use_cases.description: Structure a geo or audience holdout test with a comparable control and a longer measurement window.

prompt_templates.title: Start a simple A/B test
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an A/B test for two landing-page hero variants. Baseline conversion rate is 3%, and I need to detect a 15% lift.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a creative experiment
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a test matrix for four responsive search ad variants. Include one changed variable per variant, a primary metric, guardrails, sample size, and duration.

prompt_templates.title: Read an exported result
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my finished experiment results with sessions and conversions by variant. Report effect size, confidence interval, statistical status, and practical-effect status.

prompt_templates.title: Design an incrementality test
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a geo-holdout incrementality test for a paid campaign. Define the treatment, matched holdout, decision owner, precommitted rule, metrics, and read schedule.

output_examples.input: A landing-page test with a 3% baseline conversion rate and a 15% target lift.
output: Hypothesis: A clearer hero will increase conversion rate by at least 15%.
Design: Control and one hero-only variant with the same audience and budget logic.
Plan: State alpha, power, minimum detectable effect, required exposure, duration, and guardrails.

output_examples.input: Finished results for a control and one variant with sessions and conversions.
output: Effect: Report each conversion rate, relative lift, confidence interval, and p-value.
Decision status: Separate statistical and practical flags from the owner-approved action rule.
If the rule or owner is absent, return decision: UNDECIDED.

best_practices: Change one variable per variant and retain a control or holdout.
Precommit metrics, sample size, alpha, power, and stopping rules before reviewing results.
Name the decision owner and action rule before a test starts.
anti_patterns: Do not declare a winner from a p-value alone.
Do not stop early after repeated unplanned result checks.
Do not combine several creative or landing-page changes in one variant.

faq.question: What data do I need for a test plan?
faq.answer: Provide a baseline conversion or click rate, daily traffic, and the minimum lift worth detecting.

faq.question: What data do I need for a read-out?
faq.answer: Provide exported exposures and conversions, or equivalent metric data, for each variant.

faq.question: Can the skill choose a winner?
faq.answer: No. It reports evidence and applies an action only when a decision owner and precommitted rule are provided.

faq.question: Does it generate ad creative?
faq.answer: No. It designs and interprets experiments. Use a creative-focused skill to produce variants.

faq.question: Can it run incrementality tests?
faq.answer: It can design geo or audience holdout studies and explain the required comparison structure.

faq.question: Does it require ad-platform access?
faq.answer: No. It is designed to work with manually exported data from the user.
